lesson.title: Diminutives & Word Formation
lesson.subtitle: -je, -tje, -pje, -etje — the diminutive is Dutch's favourite word-building machine

hook.title: Shrink It and Change Its Article
hook.content: Add -je (or -tje, -pje, -etje) and a noun becomes a diminutive. Every diminutive is het, and the ending often adds affection, not just smallness: een broodje, een kopje, een huisje.

pattern.title: The ending follows the noun's shape
pattern.content: Brood → broodje, kop → kopje, huis → huisje, appel → appeltje, bloem → bloemetje, hond → hondje. The allomorph depends on the final sound; the article is always het.
pattern.linguist_note: The Dutch diminutive is a productive noun class; it marks size, affection, or simply everyday register, and always selects het.
pattern.trap_note: Do not keep the original article: de hond becomes het hondje. The diminutive overrides the noun's gender.

exercises.prompt: Match each English meaning with its Dutch twin (Diminutives & Word Formation):
exercises.target_answer: het broodje, het kopje, het huisje, het appeltje, het bloemetje, het hondje
exercises.meaning: bread roll; sandwich, small cup, little house, little apple, little flower, little dog
exercises.explanation: These are the anchors of "Diminutives & Word Formation": read each Dutch form through the pattern, not as a new word.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence says: “I have a roll.”?
exercises.explanation: “Ik heb een broodje.” is the Dutch form; the other readings bend the pattern of “Diminutives & Word Formation”.

exercises.meaning: We drink a cup of coffee.
exercises.explanation: “Wij drinken een kopje koffie.” puts the thought together the Dutch way — The ending follows the noun's shape.

diagnosis.slip: an English-shaped word order slipped in
diagnosis.cue: Do not keep the original article: de hond becomes het hondje. The diminutive overrides the noun's gender.

exercises.prompt: Which English sentence is built the Dutch way?
options: not The little house is small.
exercises.explanation: “Het huisje is klein.” is word-for-word “The little house is small.”. The odd English is the lesson — never a model to produce. Pattern: The ending follows the noun's shape.

exercises.prompt: Listen and write the whole sentence.
cues: It means: The little dog is sweet.
exercises.explanation: “Het hondje is lief.” reuses only material taught in “Diminutives & Word Formation” — The ending follows the noun's shape.
exercises.affirmation: You heard “Het hondje is lief.” — a sentence built from the lesson's own Dutch, practising The ending follows the noun's shape.

twist.prompt: One more, no safety net — say: “I see a little flower.”
twist.explanation: Bloem → bloemetje; the diminutive is het, and the ending adds affection.

summary.outcome: Form common diminutives and use het with every one.
summary.takeaway: The diminutive is a word-building machine that also resets the article to het.
